fields.name: pattern
fields.description: At the video cycle, identify the stationary marker grid and write the complete ordered list of demonstrated visited nodes, including the initial red node. Encode nodes as [row,column], using zero-based rows top to bottom and columns left to right in the front image. Follow the stick and changes in red endpoints and connecting traces chronologically. Do not add duplicates for repeated frames at one endpoint; do include genuine revisits and intermediate visited endpoints along collinear segments. During every act cycle copy the incoming list unchanged. e.g. [[2,1],[2,2],[1,2],[0,1]]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of grid nodes visited in the demonstration, including the starting node and every subsequent segment endpoint. Represent each node as [row,column], with zero-based rows from top to bottom and columns from left to right in the front image. At the video cycle, extract the entire ordered path from stick motion, newly red endpoints, and connecting traces. Repeated frames of one visit add nothing; a genuine return to a node adds another occurrence. Preserve intermediate visited endpoints even when successive segments are collinear. Carry this list unchanged through execution. e.g. [[2,1],[2,2],[1,2],[0,1]]

fields.name: reached_index
fields.description: Write 0 during the video cycle and at execution step zero: the stick starts on pattern[0]. At later act cycles, start a working index at incoming reached_index and scan the motion frames chronologically, using the current wrist image and TCP pose as additional evidence. Whenever arrival at pattern[working index + 1] is established by stick position within 1 cm and supporting endpoint activation, increment the working index and continue checking for arrival at its successor. Confirm every consecutive arrival shown, without a one-increment-per-cycle limit. Write the final working index. Proximity outside 1 cm, an action-only near-arrival allowance, or choosing an onward waypoint does not advance this field. If no steps executed, retain the incoming value. e.g. 1
fields.annotation: Zero-based index in pattern of the latest consecutively reached demonstration endpoint during execution. Write 0 at the video cycle and at the initial execution cycle, where the stick already occupies the demonstrated starting node. At subsequent cycles, scan the observed motion chronologically, starting from the carried index. Advance through every consecutive listed endpoint whose arrival is established by stick position within 1 cm and supporting endpoint activation; do not limit advancement to one endpoint per cycle. Record only confirmed arrival, not the destination being commanded or an action-only near-arrival allowance. Proximity outside 1 cm does not advance this field. Otherwise retain the previous value. If no steps execute, retain the previous value. e.g. 1

action:
During the video cycle write memory only. Execution starts with the stick already at the first demonstrated node; do not command that starting pose again. Identify the square marker grid from the current front image, using the wrist image to resolve occlusion. Its spacing is 0.10 m and its center is (x,y)=(-0.10,0). For an N-by-N grid, node [r,c] has x=-0.10+0.10*(r-(N-1)/2) and y=0.10*(c-(N-1)/2). Thus upward in the front image means decreasing world x, and rightward means increasing world y. Count actual grid rows and columns, not just currently unobscured markers. Use calibration and visible markers to check this registration.

Compute the latest strictly confirmed index by applying the memory update rule to all this cycle's motion frames, confirming every consecutive arrival shown without a one-arrival limit. Normally select the node immediately after that index. If steps have executed, the current TCP is within 0.012 m of that node's ideal waypoint, and the observed motion is consistent with finishing the segment to it, treat that one node as complete for action selection and select its successor instead. This allowance does not change reached_index, does not apply recursively, and cannot skip any other unconfirmed node. If a target remains, command exactly its ideal world x and y, z=0.070 m, retaining the current approximately downward TCP orientation. Keep the gripper closed (command -1; the stick interface ignores it). Move directly between successive demonstrated endpoints, including diagonals, without lifting, adding intermediate waypoints, or pausing to reproduce demonstration timing. Target the ideal grid coordinates rather than adding an offset to the imperfect current TCP pose. Strictly confirmed arrival or the action-only near-arrival case above is sufficient to move on; do not correct residual errors covered by these conditions.

Retry the next unconfirmed endpoint only when neither strict confirmation nor the action-only near-arrival case applies. If a motion executed no steps, do not advance progress; re-estimate the endpoint from the available images and retry a reachable, nonidentical waypoint toward it. If registration is uncertain, fit the regular 0.10 m grid to visible markers using calibration and the known current stick node, then use the best-supported next endpoint from pattern; do not invent a different pattern. Once the final endpoint is strictly confirmed or satisfies the action-only near-arrival case, make no additional tracing motion; if another response is required before automatic termination, wait a single control step to allow success evaluation.
